quote: and they no longer service our ZIP code. I don't know why, but they're not, like, we're we can't work with them anymore.
stewart_read: Customer discloses he has an existing system from a company (Namaste) that dropped his ZIP, but never says whether he owns it outright (vs. lease/PPA) or whether it's functioning. The rep never runs the orphaned_flow ownership/functioning checks.
coaching_implication: Rep should have asked 'Do you own that system outright or is it financed/leased?' and 'Is it currently working fine?' per orphaned_flow — these are hard-DQ-relevant questions that were skipped entirely on a lead who is explicitly an existing-solar customer.

quote: But right now, we have line inverters, and I'd like to switch to microinverters.
stewart_read: Customer is unusually technically fluent and specific about equipment (string vs. micro inverters, Enphase brand) — a strong buying signal of a well-researched, high-intent customer, not a typical bill-pain lead.
coaching_implication: Manager should note this lead type for the closer: technical, product-driven buyer who will want equipment-level detail, not a savings pitch. Rep correctly didn't try to explain inverter technology herself (avoided scope creep), but didn't flag the technical sophistication in the booking notes either.

quote: I can also kinda have my specialist go over the different options and and what it would look like. Because here at Ion, we we also do, like, lift and replaces.
stewart_read: This is actually the rep doing the bridge correctly — she ties the customer's past roof-replacement story to Ion's in-house lift-and-replace capability proactively, without being asked. Listed here as a positive counter-example to the usual cross_sell_miss pattern.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this move with the rep as a model — she surfaced an Ion capability at the moment it was relevant instead of either ignoring it or over-explaining it, and handed the depth to the specialist.

quote: So, you know, we're we're spending a very small amount of money on electricity, luckily, but we don't wanna spend any. So, Yeah. Exactly. And we wanna have the battery. So it's we're not looking at this from, like, a cost payback type situation.
stewart_read: Customer explicitly tells the rep the sale is not about bill savings — this is the opposite of a typical objection, but it's still a framing signal the rep should acknowledge and adapt to (e.g., resilience/backup framing instead of savings framing). Rep's response is a flat acknowledgment.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may have intentionally left this for the specialist since backup/resilience framing is closer-tier content. But the rep gives no verbal signal she registered the shift, which favors the reactive read.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to verbally mirror back non-standard buying motives ('got it, so this is really about backup and future-proofing, not the bill') — cheap, builds rapport, and hands the closer a cleaner motive than silence does.

quote: Yeah. I have well, I'm assuming you are the property owner. Is there anybody else on the title of the home with you?
stewart_read: Rep asks the co-owner question and captures the wife's name correctly, and later books the appointment while asking about scheduling for 'you and your wife' — protocol followed correctly.
coaching_implication: No coaching needed here; note as a correctly-run protocol moment for calibration reference.

quote: Yeah. Yeah. I can send you a spreadsheet. I mean, I track it in the spreadsheet.
stewart_read: Customer reveals he personally tracks his own kWh production/usage in a spreadsheet — an unusually rich data signal about buyer sophistication that the rep files as a logistics detail ('perfect, that would be awesome') rather than reflecting back or flagging for the closer.
coaching_implication: Rep could have said something like 'that's great, having your own tracked data will make the design even more precise' — small reflection that builds the customer's sense of being understood and gives the closer a stronger opening line.
